question: Suppose a sample of size n is drawn from a population with mean μ and variance σ². The standard error of x̅ is:
solution:
The correct answer is **σ/√n**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let a random sample of size n be drawn from a population with mean μ and variance σ², then
 
• The formula to calculate **the standard error of the sample mean is: SE(x̅) = σ / √n**; where: 
 
 
• σ represents the population standard deviation.
 
• n represents the sample size.
 
 
 
• The standard error of the sample mean is inversely proportional to the square root of the sample size. As the sample size increases, the standard error decreases, indicating a more precise estimate of the population mean.
 
• The standard error is useful in hypothesis testing and constructing confidence intervals for the population mean. It provides an indication of the likely range within which the true population mean lies based on the variability of sample means.
 
• In summary, the standard error of the sample mean quantifies the uncertainty associated with using the sample mean as an estimate of the population mean. It depends on the population standard deviation and the sample size, with larger sample sizes leading to smaller standard errors and more precise estimates.
